title: spawn_node coords outside i32 range wrap silently instead of failing loud
detail: strconv.parse_int accepts any i64; the i32(x)/i32(y) cast wraps silently (verified empirically: i32(5000000000) = 705032704, no error). A typo'd huge coordinate blesses a garbage topology instead of failing loud — the fail-loud discipline this PR documents for unknown node types ('an unknown type is a demo-authoring error (fail loud, never silent)'). The sibling verbs (draw/spawn ids) use parse_uint, which fails loud on overflow.
recommended_fix: Range-check x and y against the i32 bounds before the cast and return the same one-line parse error as non-numeric input (e.g. reject x/y outside -2^31..2^31-1).

title: parse_demo error returns leak the already-made dynamic arrays and cloned type_name strings
detail: Every parse_demo `return {}, ...` discards the arrays made at proc top plus any Node_Spawn type_name strings cloned before the error; run_demo and load_demo_replay free nothing on the error path. Pre-existing pattern (the older arrays leaked too), but this PR's new nodes array + clones extend it. Error-path-only, short-lived CLI.
recommended_fix: Free the partially-built Demo before each parse-error return, or parse into a caller-owned struct so run_demo/load_demo_replay can run the same cleanup defer on failure.
